entries.quantity: Small and Large Quasi-kernel Conjectures (digraphs): equivalence of sublinear bounds, and the general bounds for both

prior.value: Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture (P. L. Erdős and Székely, 1976): every n-vertex source-free digraph has a quasi-kernel Q with |Q| ≤ n/2; Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture (Spiro): every n-vertex digraph has a quasi-kernel Q with |N+[Q]| ≥ n/2. Equivalence known only for linear bounds (Spiro; Ai, Gutin, Liu and Meng arXiv:2610.23487). Best general bounds |N+[Q]| ≥ n^{2/3−o(1)} and |Q| ≤ n − n^{2/3−o(1)} (Rutschmann, arXiv:2610.29659)

new.value: for every 1/2 < β < 1, 'every n-vertex source-free digraph has a quasi-kernel with |Q| ≤ n − Ω(n^β)' is equivalent to 'every n-vertex digraph has a quasi-kernel with |N+[Q]| ≥ Ω(n^{2−1/β})'; with a refinement of Rutschmann's argument this gives |N+[Q]| ≥ n^{2/3}/64 and |Q| ≤ n − n^{3/4}/768. An equivalence (reduction) plus improved bounds; neither conjecture is resolved

entries.note: Not an Erdős problem. Checks are by the Lean community, not by the atlas. The joint statement (Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative, 2026-11-21) says dozens of people compiled the library and reproduced the same raw proof export; that a challenge file importing only Mathlib was matched to the proved theorem by comparator and by con-leche --compare; and that the inert export was accepted by Lean's kernel, by con-leche and con-ron (which come with formal soundness proofs relative to set theory) and by other independent checkers. Andrew Sutherland's verification log (MIT, checks run with Claude Code; page last updated 2026-11-23 14:35 UTC) reports all 175,187 modules compiling with zero errors; #print axioms on the five headline theorems giving only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no axioms declared outside Lean core; leanchecker replay of every module; nanoda, con-leche, con-ron and lean4lean accepting; an independent sandboxed build reproducing the export byte for byte; Lean's default kernel accepting the full export; and Comparator v4.33.0 end to end passing. At that update the lake comparator (v4.36.0) end-to-end run and one paranoid-kernel replay of the export with default settings were still running (a paranoid-kernel replay with one allocator setting changed had accepted). GRH here means Dirichlet L-functions only; Dedekind, Hecke and general automorphic L-functions are not among the checked statements. Alpöge chose to release only the Lean, so there is no readable proof yet. ProjectForty2's own rebuild did not complete (it stopped on missing compiled build files, not on a proof error), so the atlas relies on the community checks above.

prior.source: standard; framing of the paper in anthropics/formal-math vp-vnp

new.value: a claimed proof that, over every field, every arithmetic circuit for the m-variable Hamiltonian cycle polynomial, and for the m×m permanent outside characteristic 2, has more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) gates for all large m, and that the same holds for approximating circuits; hence VP is a proper subset of VNP and VNP is not contained in the closure of VP over every field. The authors say this does not settle P vs NP

entries.date_basis: repository commit date (918c8e2, merged in PR #51 the same day)

ai_involvement.detail: The README says: 'The result was discovered by an internal research Claude model. This folder holds the paper and its Lean 4 formalization. Both were written by AI models, and no human mathematician has checked the proof.' The paper (paper.pdf, 70 pages) is credited to 'Claude, Anthropic'.

entries.note: Claimed, unvetted. Not an Erdős problem (algebraic complexity). The folder has a Lean 4 formalization (lean-toolchain v4.33.1; Statement.lean imports only Mathlib, with proofs in Solution.lean). The README says: 'Lean checks the proofs, but no machine checks that this file says what is claimed', and points to Appendix Q of the paper (Table 3) for the Lean counterparts of the numbered statements and where they differ. The README's expected check is lake build plus scripts/PrintAxioms.lean naming no axioms beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and the repository CI runs Comparator against Challenge.lean with the nanoda second kernel. The atlas has not rebuilt the Lean, run the comparator, or checked that Statement.lean's definitions of VP, VNP and the closure of VP match the usual ones. No human check of the proof is cited. Repository dataset B-30.

entries.quantity: Erdős–Szekeres 'Happy Ending' function ES(n) = f(n), upper bound (Erdős #107)

prior.value: f(n) ≤ 2^{n+O(√(n log n))} (Holmsen, Mojarrad, Pach and Tardos 2020), after Suk's 2^{n+O(n^{2/3} log n)} (2017); conjecture f(n) = 2^{n-2}+1

entries.authors: Yifan Hu, Guokuan Shao, Guozhen Shen

ai_involvement.detail: The paper's title-page note says: 'The central mathematical ideas are due to the authors. The authors developed the technical approaches with the assistance of OpenAI's ChatGPT. ChatGPT was also used for proofreading.'

entries.note: A new asymptotic upper bound for Erdős #107, not a resolution: the conjecture f(n) = 2^{n-2}+1 stays open and the atlas status of #107 is unchanged. The abstract compares the result with Suk's bound; the body also cites the Holmsen–Mojarrad–Pach–Tardos bound. At retrieval (2026-11-24) erdosproblems.com/107 still names Holmsen–Mojarrad–Pach–Tardos as the current best, with 0 proof claims (last edited 11 April 2026). arXiv preprint, not refereed at retrieval; no formalisation. The atlas has not checked the proof.

entries.quantity: termination of the Kähler minimal model program with scaling (strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler klt pairs)

prior.value: termination of klt flips with scaling open in this compact Kähler setting, as framed by the authors

new.value: termination of klt flips with scaling for strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler klt pairs (X, B) with effective Q-boundary; hence such pairs have minimal models when K_X + B is pseudo-effective and Mori fibre space models otherwise

ai_involvement.detail: The comments say: 'The main result of this paper is based on the AI generated papers [OAI1] and [OAI2] and was obtained with the aid of ChatGPT.' [OAI1] and [OAI2] are OpenAI preprints of 24 September and 6 October 2026 on minimal models.

entries.note: Not an Erdős problem (algebraic geometry). The corollaries also cite further OpenAI preprints ([OAI3], [OAI4]). arXiv preprint, not refereed at retrieval; no formalisation. The atlas has not checked the proof.

entries.quantity: binary Chowla conjecture: Σ_{n≤x} μ(n)μ(n+1)

prior.value: ≪ x/(log x)^c for a tiny absolute constant c > 0 (OpenAI)

new.value: ≪_ε x/(log x)^{1−ε} for every fixed 0 < ε < 1; also Σ_{p≤x} μ(p+2) ≪_ε π(x)/(log x)^{1/2−ε}

ai_involvement.detail: The AI statement says: 'The author used ChatGPT-6 Astra for assistance writing up the article, checking, and transcribing routine adaptations of arguments. The author takes full responsibility for the correctness of the proof.' It also says the author found it helpful to discuss the earlier papers extensively with ChatGPT-6.

entries.note: Not an Erdős problem (number theory). Improves an OpenAI bound that the atlas does not index separately. arXiv preprint, not refereed at retrieval; no formalisation. The atlas has not checked the proof.

entries.quantity: limit cycles in three-dimensional competitive Lotka–Volterra systems (Gyllenberg–Yan conjecture: at least five)

prior.value: conjectured that at least five limit cycles can coexist (Gyllenberg and Yan)

new.value: a strictly competitive system with eight distinct limit cycles near one positive equilibrium, proving the conjecture; for each m = 5, 6, 7, 8 a rigorous computer-assisted proof that an explicit rational interaction matrix yields at least m hyperbolic limit cycles

entries.authors: Haoyu Albert Wang, Yuxiu Shao, Wei P. Dai

ai_involvement.detail: The abstract says: 'We thank GPT-6 Astra for helping us compare earlier constructions, identify the main obstacle to extending them, and develop the present approach.'

entries.note: Not an Erdős problem (dynamical systems). The proof is computer-assisted (interval checks), not formalised. arXiv preprint, not refereed at retrieval. The atlas has not rerun the computations.

entries.quantity: polychromatic colouring of hereditary hypergraph families: m_3 versus m_2

prior.value: m_3 ≥ 2m_2 (preceding notes in the series)

new.value: for every h ≥ 4 a hereditary family with m_2 = h and m_3 ≥ 2(h−1) + 2⌊(h−1)/3⌋ + 1 ≈ (8/3)m_2; the worst-case integrality gap of weighted transversals for m_2 ≤ h lies between h−1 and 5000h, so such families admit strong ε-nets of size at most 5000h/ε

ai_involvement.detail: The comments say: 'This paper was written by ChatGPT with very limited feedback from me.'

entries.note: Not an Erdős problem (combinatorics). Short note, not refereed at retrieval; no formalisation. The atlas has not checked the proof.

entries.quantity: linear forms in logarithms of rational numbers: ineffective measure with best-possible exponent

prior.value: case n = 1 (irrationality exponent of log a is 2) known (Liu, Jiang and Zhang, arXiv:2610.10192)

new.value: for multiplicatively independent positive rationals a_1, …, a_n and every ε > 0, |h_0 + h_1 log a_1 + … + h_n log a_n| ≥ C max(1, |h_i|)^{−n−ε} with an ineffective C > 0; the exponent n is best possible

ai_involvement.detail: The title-page note says: 'Developed with Claude (Anthropic), including mathematical exposition and formalization.' The paper says the investigation, proof development, formalization and exposition 'were carried out by Gregory V. Chudnovsky with Claude (Anthropic)', and that the method is the interpolation and determinant method of OpenAI's preprint on the irrationality exponent of π.

entries.note: Not an Erdős problem (Diophantine approximation). The abstract says the theorem and its corollary are verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib, with sources in the arXiv ancillary files built on the Lean supplement of arXiv:2610.28079; Appendix A states the formalization scope. The atlas has not rebuilt the Lean or checked statement fidelity.

entries.quantity: sup over laws μ on [0,∞) of P[X1+X2+X3 < 2X4] for iid X_i (Bellec–Fritz four-roll game; AlphaEvolve collection Problem 6.39)

prior.value: lower bound 0.4006953723… (construction), conjectured exact by Bellec and Fritz; upper bounds from exchangeability only

new.value: the supremum equals 0.4006953723…, proving the Bellec–Fritz conjecture via a flag-algebra semidefinite certificate with ratio cutoffs on four sample points; exact values of S_2(c), S_3(c) on several intervals and an answer to Bellec–Fritz Problem 5.3

ai_involvement.detail: Section 2 ('AI usage and verification') says: 'Under human guidance and supervision, frontier AI models have been used extensively to derive the results of this paper, including theorem statements, proofs, and numerical code for finding useful SDP certificates.' No model is named.

entries.note: Not an Erdős problem (probability). The paper says Theorem 1.1 (the exact value) is formalized in Lean 4, covering the probability argument and the finite certificate checks; the other bounds rest on the written proofs and exact certificate checks. Certificates, verifiers and the Lean proof are in github.com/antalez/flag-algebras-iid (MIT, created 2026-11-24) and the arXiv ancillary files. The atlas has not rebuilt the Lean or rerun the certificates.
